steps.description: Click the "Teams Agents and Apps" option in the "New Project" modal dropdown within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit interface, as indicated by the red crosshair at coordinates (290, 230).
Click the "General Teams Agent" option in the dropdown menu within the "Teams Agent or App Using Microsoft Teams SDK" dialog in Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit on Visual Studio Code.

Click the "Simple Bot" option in the "Teams Capability" dropdown within Visual Studio Code’s Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit interface, selecting a template described as "A simple implementation of an echo bot that's ready for customization."
Click the "TypeScript" option in the "Programming Language" dropdown within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension interface in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Default folder" text field in the "Workspace Folder" dialog within Microsoft Visual Studio Code to select the project location for Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.
Click the "Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit" item in the Visual Studio Code Explorer sidebar to select it, as indicated by the red crosshair at position (26, 311) and the tooltip displaying its name.
Press the F1 key to open the command palette in Visual Studio Code, while the main workspace and the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit side panel are visible.
Type the text 'focus on environment view' into the Visual Studio Code command palette input field at the top center of the application window.
Click the "Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit: Focus on Environment View" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette dropdown, located at the top center of the interface.
@assertion there is the message "Sign in with your correct ..." in the dev ENVIRONMENT section
Click the "Manage Microsoft 365 App (with Microsoft Entra app) Collaborators" button next to the "dev" environment in the MICROSOFT 365 AGENTS TOOLKIT panel in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Add App Owners" option in the command palette dropdown within the Visual Studio Code interface, under the context "Manage who can make changes to your app."
Click the "app Your app" option in the pop-up dialog titled "Select the app for which you want to manage collaborators" within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "OK" button in the app selection dialog to confirm the chosen Microsoft Entra app for managing collaborators in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "manifest.json" file option in the "Select Teams manifest.json File" dialog within Visual Studio Code, highlighting the file path selection for a Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit workflow.
@assertion there is pop up window to sign in.
Click the "Cancel" button in the Microsoft 365 developer sandbox prompt at the top of the Visual Studio Code interface.

Click the "dev" environment entry in the MICROSOFT 365 AGENTS TOOLKIT panel of Visual Studio Code, triggering the tooltip "Manage Microsoft 365 App (with Microsoft Entra app) Collaborators" for environment management.

Click the "List App Owners" option in the Visual Studio Code command palette under the prompt "Manage who can make changes to your app". The selection is highlighted in the dropdown, and the interface is part of the Microsoft 365 Agents extension within VS Code.
Click the "app" option in the dropdown list within the "Select the app for which you want to manage collaborators" dialog in the Microsoft 365 Agents extension panel of Visual Studio Code.
Click the "OK" button in the dialog titled "Select the app for which you want to manage collaborators" within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension of Visual Studio Code.
Click the "manifest.json" file entry in the "Select Teams manifest.json File" dialog within Visual Studio Code.
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code, with the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension panel active.
Type the text “>show notification” into the VS Code Command Palette input box to search for the “Notifications: Show Notifications” command.
Click on the "Notifications: Show Notification" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette after searching for "show notification".
Click the "Expand Notification (Right Arrow)" button in the Notifications panel of Visual Studio Code to view the full error message: "[Core.l]: Unable to load manifest id from path: ...".
@assertion there is a notification to remind to provision.
Press the F1 key to open the command palette in Visual Studio Code with the "MICROSOFT 365 AGENTS TOOLKIT" extension active, providing access to commands related to agent and app development.
Type the text "clear notification" into the Visual Studio Code command palette input field to filter and highlight the "Notifications: Clear All Notifications" command.
Click the "Notifications: Clear All Notifications" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette, highlighted in blue after searching for ">clear notification".
Click the "Manage Microsoft 365 App (with Microsoft Entra app) Collaborators" button next to the "dev (Provisioned)" environment in the MICROSOFT 365 AGENTS TOOLKIT panel of Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Add App Owners" option in the "Manage who can make changes to your app" dropdown dialog of the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension in Visual Studio Code.

Click the "app You" entry in the application selection dropdown within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit interface in Visual Studio Code, under the prompt "Select the app for which you want to manage collaborators."

Click the blue plus (+) button next to "1 Selected" in the "Select the app for which you want to manage collaborators" dialog within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension, inside Visual Studio Code.
Click the "manifest.json" file entry in the "Select Teams manifest.json File" dialog in Visual Studio Code.
Select all text in the email input field of the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app" dialog within Visual Studio Code by pressing Ctrl+A.

Type 'invalidemail@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com' into the email input field in the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app for the account under the same Microsoft 365 tenant (email)" dialog within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension panel in Visual Studio Code.

Click the red "X" button next to the invalid email address input field in the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app" dialog within the Visual Studio Code Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension, to clear the entered email address.

Press the Enter key to submit the email address "invalidemail@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com" in the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app" input dialog within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension for Visual Studio Code.
@assertion the notification "CannotFindUserInCurrentTenant" exists
Click the "Manage Microsoft 365 App (with Microsoft Entra app) Collaborators" button for the "dev (Provisioned)" environment in the MICROSOFT 365 AGENTS TOOLKIT side panel of Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Add App Owners" option in the dropdown under "Manage who can make changes to your app" within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension in Visual Studio Code.

Click the "Agent Microsoft 365 Agent" option in the app selection dropdown within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit interface in Visual Studio Code. The red crosshair marks the exact interaction point, ensuring the "Agent" app option is selected for managing collaborators.
Click the “Manage collaborators” blue button (with user icon) in the app selection popup of the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "manifest.json" file option in the dropdown list within the "Select Teams manifest.json File" dialog of Visual Studio Code.
Select all text in the email input field of the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app" dialog at the top of the Visual Studio Code interface.

Type text into the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app" email input field in Visual Studio Code, entering the owner’s email address in the format `[UserName]@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com` at the top prompt bar.

Type the email address "test002@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com" into the input field of the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app" prompt within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension in Visual Studio Code.

Press the Enter key to confirm the email input (test002@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com) in the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app" dialog within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension for Visual Studio Code.

Press the Enter key to confirm the email input (test002@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com) in the "Add owner to Teams/Microsoft Entra app" dialog within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit interface in Visual Studio Code.
@assertion the notification "Added account" exists
Press the F1 key to open the command palette in Visual Studio Code, within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension workspace.
Type "clear notification" into the Visual Studio Code command palette input field to search for and execute the "Notifications: Clear All Notifications" command.
Click the "Notifications: Clear All Notifications" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette to clear notifications.
Press the F1 key to open the command palette in Visual Studio Code while the "MICROSOFT 365 AGENTS TOOLKIT" extension panel is active.
Type the text 'environment view' into the Visual Studio Code command palette input box at the top center of the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit workspace interface.

Click the "Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit: Focus on Environment View" command in the VS Code command palette dropdown, located at the top-center of the Visual Studio Code interface, to select and execute the command.

Click the "Manage Microsoft 365 App (with Microsoft Entra app) Collaborators" button for the "dev (Provisioned)" environment in the ENVIRONMENT panel of the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension within Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Add App Owners" option in the "Manage who can make changes to your app" dropdown within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension panel in Visual Studio Code.

Click the "app YHP" option in the selection dropdown within the "Select the app for which you want to manage collaborators" dialog in Visual Studio Code, under the Microsoft 365 Agents extension panel.
Click the "OK" button in the app selection dialog to confirm the chosen app for managing collaborators within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "manifest.json" entry in the file selection dropdown within the "Select Teams manifest.json File" dialog in Visual Studio Code.
@assertion there are two App Owners that listed in the output window
Press the F1 key to open the command palette in Visual Studio Code, within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit workspace.
Type the text "accounts" into the Visual Studio Code Command Palette input field to trigger command search suggestions.
Click the "Microsoft 365 Agents: Accounts" entry in the VS Code command palette to select this command from the filtered search results.
Click the “Sign out of Microsoft 365: ${{env:M365_ACCOUNT_NAME}}” option in the account command dropdown within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension panel in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Sign out" button in the confirmation dialog to sign out of the account '${{env:M365_ACCOUNT_NAME}}' within the Visual Studio Code Microsoft 365 extension interface.
@assertion notification "Successfully signed out" exists
Press the F1 key to open the Visual Studio Code command palette within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit workspace.
Type text 'accounts' into the VS Code command palette input box to filter and display related commands and views.
Click the "Microsoft 365 Agents: Account" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette, located under the search input after entering ">accounts".
Click the "Sign in to Microsoft 365" option in the account selection dropdown within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension panel in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Sign in" button in the Microsoft 365 developer sandbox prompt within Visual Studio Code to begin authentication.

Click the "Use another account" option in the Microsoft account picker dialog on the login.microsoftonline.com sign-in page using Google Chrome. The click targets the area with a plus icon and label, below the listed account choices.
Paste clipboard content into the "Email or phone" input field on the Microsoft sign-in page within Google Chrome.
Click on the "Email or phone" input field in the Microsoft sign-in form on the login.microsoftonline.com page within Google Chrome.
Enter the email address 'test002@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com' into the Microsoft login page's username/email input field in Google Chrome, directly above the 'Next' button on the 'Sign in' screen.
Click the "Next" button on the Microsoft sign-in page, positioned to the right of the "Back" button after entering the username test002@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com in Google Chrome.
Type text ${{env:M365_ACCOUNT_PASSWORD}} into the password input field on the Microsoft sign-in page for user test002@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com within a Chrome browser window.
Click the "Sign in" button on the Microsoft login page in Google Chrome after entering the password for the account test002@xxbdw.onmicrosoft.com.
Click the "Close" (X) button at the top-right corner of the Chrome browser window to close the "Visual Studio Code - You are signed in now and can close this page" tab.
@assertion notification "Successfully signed in to Microsoft 365 account" exists
Click the "Manage Microsoft 365 App (with Microsoft Entra app) Collaborators" button for the "dev (Provisioned)" environment in the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit sidebar within Visual Studio Code.

Click the "List App Owners" option in the command palette dropdown within the Visual Studio Code extension for Microsoft 365 Agents. This action lists all the owners who can make changes to your Teams and Microsoft Entra app registrations.
Click the checkbox next to "app YH APP" in the "Select the app for which you want to manage collaborators" dialog within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "OK" button in the "Select the app for which you want to manage collaborators" dialog within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "manifest.json" file option in the "Select Teams manifest.json File" dialog within the Microsoft Visual Studio Code application.
@assertion there are two App Owners that listed in the output window
Press the F1 key to open the command palette in Visual Studio Code while the "Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit" extension panel is active.
Type text 'provision' into the Visual Studio Code command palette textbox to search for commands within the Microsoft 365 Agents extension.
Select the "Microsoft 365 Agents: Provision" command from the Visual Studio Code command palette by clicking on its entry at coordinates (440, 59).
Click the "Provision" button in the confirmation dialog prompting to provision resources for the selected Azure and Microsoft 365 accounts within the Visual Studio Code interface.

Press the F1 key in the Visual Studio Code window with the "MICROSOFT 365 AGENTS TOOLKIT" extension panel active, to open the Command Palette and access developer commands specific to the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit context.
Type 'show notification' into the Visual Studio Code command palette input field at the top center of the interface.
Click the "Notifications: Show Notification" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette dropdown to select it.
@assertion notification 'provision stage executed successfully' exist.
